blocks.title: A conjecture
blocks.content:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. Denote by $J_N(K;q)$ the colored Jones polynomial associated to the $N$-dimensional irreducible representation of the Lie algebra $sl(2,\mathbb{C})$ [@Kirillov/Reshetikhin:1989]. We normalize it so that $J_2(K;q)$ is the Jones polynomial [@Jones:BULAM385] and that $J_N(U;q)=1$, where $U$ is the unknot.

We propose the following conjecture as a version of the volume conjecture.

blocks.title: Front matter
blocks.content:
arXiv:math/0603217v3  [math.GT]  15 Apr 2006
A VERSION OF THE VOLUME CONJECTURE
HITOSHI MURAKAMI
Abstract. We propose a version of the volume conjecture that would relate a
certain limit of the colored Jones polynomials of a knot to the volume function
deﬁned by a representation of the fundamental group of the knot complement
to the special linear group of degree two over complex numbers.
We also
conﬁrm the conjecture for the ﬁgure-eight knot and torus knots. This version
is diﬀerent from S. Gukov’s because of a choice of polarization.

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.content:
In this section we prove Conjecture [\[conj:parameterization\]](#conj:parameterization){reference-type="ref" reference="conj:parameterization"} for torus knots. (To be honest, [\[eq:volume\]](#eq:volume){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:volume"} is proved only up to a constant, that is, we prove [\[eq:Schlafli\]](#eq:Schlafli){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:Schlafli"} instead.)
